name: Marked Reduction Test for Proper Obstructions in an Expansion
statement:
Let $X\subseteq Q_{F\cup\{e\}}$ be ample, use all $n+1$ displayed coordinates, and have both $e$-sections and its $e$-contraction dismantlable ample. Put $O=X^{\{e\}}$. Every ample forbidden proper pc-minor $H$ of $X$ can be written $H=
u X$, where the nonempty minor sequence $
u$ uses only coordinates in $F$, leaves $e$ active, and satisfies $H^{\{e\}}=
u O$. If $O$ is forbidden and uses all of $F$, then $
u O$ is dismantlable ample. If $H$ has $n$ active coordinates, $
u$ is one elementary operation, so the orders of the coordinate reductions of $H$ and of the elementary pc-minors of $O$ must have a common value.
proof: Any operation deleting $e$ can be commuted to the start of a minor sequence; the result would then be a pc-minor of a positive $e$-section or contraction, contradicting that $H$ is forbidden. The coordinate $e$ cannot become constant for the same reason. Old-coordinate restrictions commute with reduction in $e$. For contraction, isometry supplies an intermediate vertex whenever projected $e$-mates come from opposite shores, giving $(\pi_qX)^{\{e\}}=\pi_qO$; iteration proves $H^{\{e\}}=\nu O$. If $O$ is forbidden and uses every old coordinate, the first operation is proper on $O$, so forbidden-minor minimality makes $\nu O$ positive. Retaining $n$ active coordinates permits exactly one nontrivial elementary operation, which yields the cardinality intersection test.
comments: The cardinality intersection is necessary only; it is not an inverse-construction criterion.
